title: Provider pricing override layer for dsh-model-pricing
description: Per-provider (billing-channel) pricing over the model base table, WITH a time dimension. Each channel declares its FORM (`providers[].form`: official / relay / subscription / wrapper) and, unless it is a wrapper, a billing nature plus a list of entries. Each entry resolves to one of: (a) a reference to a base-table model whose full price history is inherited (the channel tracks the official/vendor price, including past price changes), or (b) an explicit timeline of [from, to) rate segments (the channel has its own price history, e.g. a relay or an unknown model the user prices by hand). Billing nature belongs to the CHANNEL (`providers[].billing`) and is the default for every entry of that channel; an entry may override it. This keeps REAL metered spend apart from SUBSCRIPTION value. A WRAPPER is a plugin-minted synthetic twin of another route: it names that route in `aliasOf` and carries no billing and no entries of its own — it inherits both, and is never priced separately.

version.description: Bump when pricing semantics change; consumers re-fetch on change.

updatedAt.description: Unix seconds of the last content change (a no-op rebuild keeps it).

currency.description: All amounts are RMB per million tokens. Required: consumers reject a feed that is not RMB. The USD rate is NOT carried here: it is the base table's single source of truth.

provider.description: Provider route key as recorded in the ledger (e.g. deepseek-official, opencode-go, commandcode, zai, staryears). A plugin-minted wrapper id (modlens-commandcode, deepseek-modlens) is a synthetic twin of the route it wraps, not a channel of its own: same operator, same billing class, same inherited base — declared with `form: wrapper` + `aliasOf`.

form.description: How this channel is operated and priced. official: the vendor's own metered API (the channel operator IS the model vendor). relay: a third party's metered channel priced at its own rate, possibly marked up. subscription: model access bundled in a plan, not billed per token. wrapper: a client plugin's synthetic twin of another route in this feed — it never prices anything itself. Display metadata for consumers (grouping/annotation); the pricing rule that rides on it is only that a wrapper carries no entries.

billing.description: The CHANNEL's billing nature, the default for every entry below. metered: a REAL per-token spend (official API or relay/reseller at its own rate). subscription: included in a plan — the value it creates equals the metered-equivalent rates, NOT actual spend. Consumers must keep these apart when summing. Absent on a wrapper, which inherits its target's nature.

aliasOf.description: The channel this wrapper is a synthetic twin of. Its entries, billing nature and label are inherited wholesale, so a vendor price change still needs one edit only. Only for form: wrapper; the target must be a non-wrapper channel of this same feed. Consumers materialize it as a one-hop route alias (the wrapper's own entries, if a consumer's hand layer adds any, still win).

model.description: Exact model string as recorded under this provider (may carry a provider prefix, e.g. deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash).

billing.description: Per-entry override of the channel's billing nature, for a mixed channel. Omit to inherit `providers[].billing`.

inheritBase.description: When present, this (provider, model) follows the base table's FULL price history of the named modelId — every time rule / context tier / peak slot, past and present. Official/direct channels and subscription channels valued at official prices use this, so a vendor price change needs no edit here. Mutually exclusive with segments.

segments.description: An explicit price history when the channel has its OWN rates (a relay's real prices). Mutually exclusive with inheritBase. Segments tile the full timeline: the first starts at 0 (or omits `from`), the last is open-ended (omits `to`). Rates are FLAT per segment — a channel's own peak windows / context tiers cannot be expressed; use inheritBase to follow the official rule set instead.

from.description: Segment start, inclusive, Unix seconds. Defaults to the previous segment's to (or 0 for the first).

to.description: Segment end, EXCLUSIVE, Unix seconds. Omit on the last segment (open-ended).

note.description: What changed in this segment (e.g. 'relay raised price').

placeholder.description: Relay placeholder: the inherited base price stands in until the user fills real segments. Only meaningful with inheritBase.

note.description: Human note (terms reference, caveat, date checked).
